speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever or acute distress. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly where it hurts and what you were doing right before the limp started?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the pain is localized to the left knee but the limp suggests the problem may be higher up. Given the child's age and lack of trauma, could you tell me if he has noticed any pain or stiffness in his left hip or groin?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).

While I have already received the critical details that this 7-year-old male presents with a limp, left knee pain, and no trauma or fever—classic signs of SCFE where hip pathology refers pain to the knee—I will not ask further questions. I require imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_X-Ray_AP_and_Lateral.
